expected_flag: `set -o pipefail` set in the OUTER script does NOT propagate into the subshell created by parentheses; the subshell inherits the script's variables but each subshell has its own pipefail setting. The exit status of `(cmd1 | cmd2)` is the status of cmd2, masking failures in cmd1. Fix: add `set -o pipefail` inside the subshell, or use `${PIPESTATUS[@]}` to inspect, or restructure to avoid the subshell.

mutable default argument: `def append_log(msg, sink=[])` shares the SAME list across all calls that don't pass `sink`; logs from different invocations leak into each other. Fix: use `sink=None` and create a fresh list inside if `sink is None`.

expected_flag: loop-variable capture in goroutines: in pre-Go-1.22 code (and still a footgun even after), `for i, item := range items { go func() { use(item) }() }` captures `item` by reference; all goroutines see the LAST value. Fix: pass as argument `go func(it Item) { use(it) }(item)`, or shadow with `item := item` inside the loop body, or upgrade to Go 1.22+ where each iteration has its own scope.

deadlock pattern: holding a `Mutex` guard across an `.await` (or across another lock acquisition that the current thread might already hold transitively). The function locks `cache`, then calls `compute_value` which itself tries to lock `cache` again — same-thread re-entry on a non-reentrant Mutex deadlocks. Fix: drop the guard before calling out, or restructure so the inner function doesn't need the lock, or use a reader-writer lock with care.

`target="_blank"` without `rel="noopener noreferrer"` is a tabnabbing risk: the opened page can use `window.opener` to navigate the source tab to a phishing page (older browsers) and leaks Referer (without `noreferrer`). Fix: add `rel="noopener noreferrer"` (or at minimum `noopener`). Modern browsers default to `noopener` for `target="_blank"` but an explicit attribute is best practice.

expected_flag: `z-index` only takes effect on positioned elements (position other than `static`). Without `position: relative` (or absolute/fixed/sticky), the `z-index: 9999` on `.tooltip` is silently ignored — the tooltip will not stack above the rest of the document. Fix: add `position: relative` (or whichever positioning matches the tooltip's layout intent).

`setTimeout(fn, 0)` to 'fix' a race condition just defers the bug — it doesn't synchronize anything, it relies on event-loop ordering that breaks under load or in different runtimes. The real fix is to wait for the dependency explicitly: await a promise that resolves when the data is loaded, listen for the relevant event, or refactor so the consumer is invoked AFTER the producer finishes.

expected_flag: TOCTOU race: between `mktemp` returning a path and `mv $TMPDIR $DEST` running, another process can replace `$TMPDIR` (e.g. via symlink) and the mv lands somewhere unintended. Use `mktemp -d` + immediate use, OR `mv -T` (refuse-if-target-exists), OR write directly to a final-location temp file under the destination dir.

expected_flag: data race: dict reads in one thread overlap with writes in another. CPython's GIL makes individual dict ops atomic, but compound operations like `if key in d: d[key].append(...)` are NOT — between the check and the append the dict can mutate. Use a threading.Lock around the compound op, or use collections.defaultdict + threading-safe primitives.

concurrent map access is a runtime panic in Go (`fatal error: concurrent map read and map write`). The detector triggers on simultaneous read+write or write+write. Fix: protect with sync.Mutex (or sync.RWMutex if reads dominate), or switch to sync.Map for the simple-cache case.

holding a `std::sync::MutexGuard` (or any non-Send guard) across an `.await` point in async code can deadlock — the guard can be held across a task swap onto a different thread and another task waiting for the lock will never progress. Fix: drop the guard before the await (introduce a scope, or call `drop(guard)` explicitly), or use `tokio::sync::Mutex` whose guard is Send-safe across awaits.

`autocomplete="off"` on individual inputs is largely ignored by modern browsers for password fields (they use heuristics + saved-credentials anyway). For genuinely-sensitive non-password fields use `autocomplete="new-password"` or `autocomplete="one-time-code"`. For login forms accept that browser password managers WILL participate; design accordingly.

expected_flag: `100vh` on mobile browsers does NOT match the visible viewport — it includes the URL bar / browser chrome area, so a `100vh` element overflows the bottom by the URL-bar height when the bar is visible. Modern fix: use `100dvh` (dynamic viewport height). Older fallback: track `window.innerHeight` in JS and set a CSS variable.

missing `await` on `save(user)` — the function returns a Promise but the caller doesn't await or .then it. The console.log fires before save completes; if save rejects, it becomes an unhandled rejection (warning today, will be a fatal exit in future Node). Fix: `await save(user)` (and propagate the async). If you genuinely want fire-and-forget, attach `.catch(handler)` to make the rejection explicit.

expected_flag: silent partial-write on disk full / quota / permissions: `cmd > out.txt` with `set -e` does NOT propagate the redirection failure if `cmd` exits 0 but the redirection runs out of disk mid-write — `set -e` only catches command exits, not write errors. Use `cmd > out.txt && sync && [ -s out.txt ] || die`, write to a tmpfile + atomic rename via `mv`, or check size/checksum after; use `dd status=progress` if the volume warrants it. The deeper issue: shell-redirection error handling needs explicit checking.

expected_flag: context.Background() in a request handler ignores the request's deadline/cancellation — when the client disconnects or the upstream times out, this DB query keeps running and consumes a connection. Use `r.Context()` (or a derived ctx with the right deadline) so the query gets cancelled. The same applies to any I/O the handler kicks off — db, downstream HTTP, message bus.

writing to the lock guard inside `iter()` causes a deadlock or borrow-check failure; in this code specifically the spawned tokio task captures `cache` and the outer task ALSO holds it — same-process re-entry on a tokio Mutex is fine, but the issue is the GROWING vec inside the held guard plus the .await inside the loop body would hold the lock across the await and starve other readers. Fix: clone what you need (item id), drop the guard, then await; or use a more granular lock per-key.

`<form action="/transfer" method="GET">` for a state-changing operation: GET requests are logged, cached by browsers, indexed by referers, included in browser history. Use POST for state changes. Plus: this form has no CSRF token (no anti-forgery defence) and no `autocomplete="off"` semantics for sensitive amount fields (which is its own can of worms — see expert-review-html).

expected_flag: animating `top` triggers layout (reflow + repaint + composite) on every frame, causing jank on scroll and battery drain on mobile. Animate `transform: translateY(...)` instead — the GPU can compose this without recalculating layout. Same applies to `left`/`width`/`height`/`margin` — prefer `transform` and `opacity` for smooth animations.

`localStorage` is synchronous and runs on the main thread — large reads/writes block paint. It's also unencrypted and accessible to any script on the same origin; storing auth tokens or PII there is a known XSS-amplification anti-pattern. For session tokens use httpOnly cookies; for app state >100KB use IndexedDB (async); for small UI-only state localStorage is fine but keep payloads small.
